definitions.explanation: Requiring payment; not free. Used to describe services, facilities, or content that cost money.

examples.japanese: この{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}は{有料|ゆうりょう}です。
examples.english: This parking lot charges a fee.

examples.japanese: {有料|ゆうりょう}コンテンツを{購入|こうにゅう}した。
{有料|ゆうりょう}{道路|どうろ}を{通|とお}った。

notes:
{有料|ゆうりょう} means "requiring payment" — the opposite of {無料|むりょう} (free). It functions as a noun and の-adjective, modifying other nouns directly or with の.

COMPOUND:
{有|ゆう} (have/exist) + {料|りょう} (fee) — literally "fee exists."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有料|ゆうりょう}{道路|どうろ}: toll road
- {有料|ゆうりょう}{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}: paid parking
- {有料|ゆうりょう}サービス: paid service
- {有料|ゆうりょう}コンテンツ: paid content
- {有料|ゆうりょう}アプリ: paid app
- {有料|ゆうりょう}{会員|かいいん}: paid member

PATTERN:
{有料|ゆうりょう} often appears in signs and notices: この{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}は{有料|ゆうりょう}です (This parking lot charges a fee). In everyday speech, the contrast with {無料|むりょう} is very common: {有料|ゆうりょう}か{無料|むりょう}か (whether it's paid or free).
